title: An involution of the interval $[0,\tfrac12]$
statement: Let $\delta$ be a real number with $0 \le \delta \le \tfrac12$, and define $\tau = \tfrac12 - \sqrt{\delta(1-\delta)}$. Then $\tau$ again lies in $[0,\tfrac12]$ and applying the same rule to it recovers $\delta$, that is, $\tfrac12 - \sqrt{\tau(1-\tau)} = \delta$. Hence the map $x \mapsto \tfrac12 - \sqrt{x(1-x)}$ is an involution of the interval $[0,\tfrac12]$.
